newsitem.title: USA: Oppenheimer holds 6.97 pct Chateau stake.
newsitem.headline: Oppenheimer holds 6.97 pct Chateau stake.

text.p: Oppenheimer & Co Inc said Friday it has acquired a 6.97 percent stake in Chateau Properties Inc for $11.1 million and is urging the company to form an independent directors' committee to represent shareholders in considering offers to acquire Chateau.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Oppenheimer said it is not aligned with any particular bidder for Chateau and that its stake was acquired in the ordinary course of its business and "not for the purpose of acquiring control of the company."
"We are delighted to see that the company's properties are so attractive that they have enticed at least three parties to make merger proposals or tender offers..." Oppenheimer said.

It said that, to avoid chilling current and potential interest in the company, the Chateau board should adopt a resolution confirming that the ownership limit and excess stock provisions in Chateau's articles serve only to satisfy the so-called concentrated ownership rule.
Morever, the resolution should provide that shares purchased through a tender offer by any successul bidder that is a "look through entity" will not be deemed excess stock, it said.
Oppenheimer said it made its position known in a letter to Chateau on Friday (September 13) addressed to the company's chairman, John Boll. A copy was included in the filing.
According to the filing, Oppenheimer holds 425,000 common shares of Chateau, a Clinton Township, Mich.,-based real estate investment trust.
The firm bought the stake between August 19 and September 13 at prices ranging from $25.3438 to $26.75 a share.
On September 4, Chateau Properties said it continues to consider unsolicited offers for the company.
